target_customer: Employers and gig platforms that screen workers, later mortgage lenders, landlords and insurers
problem: Background checks were slow, manual and opaque, which hurt hiring speed for on-demand companies and fairness for candidates.
business_model: Usage-based API and per-check pricing with enterprise contracts
product_category: Background screening API and HR tech

founders.name: Daniel Yanisse
founders.background_notes: Software engineer at several startups before Checkr per YC page.

founders.name: Jonathan Perichon
founders.background_notes: Worked with Yanisse as an engineer at on-demand delivery startup Deliv.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building an API on top of fragmented county, state and federal record sources and meeting FCRA compliance was standard engineering with hard data integration parts.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance know-how and data source integrations took years, and embedding in platform hiring flows created switching costs, but incumbents could copy the API wrapper.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Legacy screeners stayed slower and less API oriented per later comparisons; Sterling was bought by First Advantage in 2024, while Checkr remained independent and private.

market_need_then: On-demand platforms such as Deliv, where the founders worked, needed fast, high volume worker screening, and the founders saw the incumbent process as antiquated.

branding.domain_note: Uses checkr.com; acquisition history not found

identity.logo: Lowercase sans serif wordmark in aqua, navy or white, with a monogram for small uses
identity.visual_style: Clean and modern; refreshed in July 2022 to be free of ornament
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, benefit led, short punchy headlines, direct second person address

branding.brand_signature: Fair chance hiring commitment and the lowercase wordmark

rebrands.to: Refreshed logo, photography, typography and colors
rebrands.why: Company said the brand needed a refresh to evoke trust, transparency and humility.

branding.community_and_virality: Fair Chance Month campaigns and fairness commitments; no evidence of fan community or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in HR tech and gig platforms with a company claim of 140,000 plus businesses, but the brand is B2B and no independent brand coverage beyond the 2022 refresh was found.

outcome_analysis: Checkr rode the growth of gig platforms that needed fast API based screening, raising a reported 160 million dollar Series D at 2.2 billion in 2019 and a 250 million dollar Series E at 4.6 billion in 2021 before expanding to mortgage, tenant and insurance screening. It stayed private and independent, faced FCRA litigation including a 2019 settlement headline, and the main risk is regulation and accuracy disputes rather than competition.
notes: Competitor list left empty: the dated competitor search returned only 2024 to 2026 comparison pages, nothing near the 2014 batch. A 100M Series C in April 2018 led by T. Rowe Price appears in one snippet only and is unverified, so it is not a round. Sacra reports a 120M Series E-II in April 2022 at 5.75B and CB Insights lists a 2025 E-III of 61.1M, both single source and unverified. Totals range from 679M to 740M across aggregators. A Salestools page claiming a 500M Series E led by Silver Lake is uncorroborated. Series A and B and the seed are not documented. Company scale claims on its website are its own.
